title: Naruto: Rise of a Ninja
subtitle: A familiar village becomes somewhere to explore

body: Naruto: Rise of a Ninja is Ubisoft Montreal's Xbox 360 action-adventure, released in North America on 30 October 2007. It follows the early anime story through Naruto's development as a young ninja, combining an explorable three-dimensional environment with one-on-one fighting. The player crosses rooftops, completes tasks and earns money for improvements before entering encounters presented through a more focused combat system. The cel-shaded characters and locations connect those activities to the animated series, allowing the village to function as a place the player learns rather than simply a background behind successive fights.

Platforming and races test Naruto's movement through the environment, while encounters shift into a fighting-game arrangement of attacks, combinations and special moves. New abilities expand the available responses as the story progresses. The player returns to familiar places with a greater command of the character, connecting improvement in combat to the broader adventure. Tasks and upgrades give exploration a practical purpose between major confrontations. This alternation keeps the story moving through different kinds of activity: understanding a route across the village can matter before the next opponent needs to be defeated.

Rise of a Ninja was the first Naruto game developed by a non-Japanese company and drew specifically on the English-dubbed anime. Its adventure covers the story through the Invasion of Konoha arc. A separate fighting mode offered local contests and Xbox Live competition, with downloadable characters expanding the roster after release. Ubisoft followed it with The Broken Bond in 2008. The original's distinctive choice was to place familiar fighting encounters inside a navigable world, giving the player time to inhabit Naruto's surroundings between the events and rivalries that define the series.
